summary: Initial security due-diligence call. Maravista is evaluating Redwood for a mix of hosted (customer edges) and private deployment. Main concerns: auditability, ability to use their AWS KMS, SSO integration with Okta, explaining RBAC model and retention controls. Agreed to follow up with SOC2 artifacts and a technical deep dive focused on private deployment network diagrams and KMS flow.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-03-05 14:00 UTC | Duration: 53m | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Ellen Park (Maravista Head Eng), Diego Marquez (Maravista Security Architect), Sonia Patel (Maravista PM)

00:00 Jordan Lee: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, um we'll just do quick intros then dive into the security items you flagged in the intake form
00:10 Ellen Park: yeah thanks, appreciate it. we're in the middle of a procurement window so keeping this tight. main ask is: can we run some inference on customer PII and still comply with our retention requirements.
00:25 Priya Raman: got it. quick note - we usually recommend segregating PII processing to Dedicated or Private depending on your residency needs, but hosted can be ok with certain controls.
00:40 Diego Marquez: ok, when you say controls can you be specific? encryption at rest, key ownership, that sort of thing. we have a corporate mandate to use our AWS KMS for all keys.
00:52 Priya Raman: yes, we support customer-managed keys in both Dedicated and Private. Hosted has a bring-your-own-key flow for enterprise accounts via KMS, there are some audit API constraints, i'll detail those in the doc.
01:05 Sonia Patel: is the BYOK live today or still in beta? we can't commit without full key rotation story.
01:12 Jordan Lee: it's production for most enterprise customers; there's a few edge cases for very old model variants where we need to coordinate, but in general rotation and envelope encryption are supported.
01:25 Diego Marquez: ok, can you describe the key flow? do tokens ever touch Redwood's master key? our legal team will ask.
01:35 Priya Raman: high-level, with customer-managed KMS we perform envelope encryption: customer key encrypts WRAP key, Redwood stores wrapped key. plaintext keys are never persisted. during runtime the wrapped key is unwrapped transiently only on hosts that are part of the Private or Dedicated pool, and HSM protections are applied. i'll draw a diagram in the tech deep dive.
01:55 Ellen Park: that's useful but we need sample diagrams for our security review board; can you supply network and flow diagrams with ports and subnets?
02:07 Jordan Lee: absolutely, Priya will prepare Private deployment network diagrams showing VPC peering, NACLs, subnets, and bastion patterns.
02:14 Diego Marquez: next: audit logs. we need immutable, tamper-evident logs for inference requests and admin actions, retention 2 years, and export to our SIEM.
02:26 Priya Raman: we emit audit logs for token provisioning, model rollouts, admin actions, and request-level metadata. For Dedicated and Private, logs can be forwarded to your CloudWatch/Splunk via an agent or syslog endpoint. For Hosted, we offer an export endpoint but you may not get request body-level detail unless you enable paid retention.
02:44 Sonia Patel: request-level detail meaning prompt text? that's PII risk for us.
02:50 Priya Raman: right. prompt-level logging is opt-in. we recommend hashing or redaction for PII. Also Redwood Optimize has a separate pipeline for evals which is isolated.
03:05 Ellen Park: okay. SOC 2 evidence — do you have a SOC 2 Type II report and scope?
03:12 Jordan Lee: yes, we completed SOC 2 Type II last year; we also have ISO 27001 certification in scope for our control plane. i'll attach the redacted report. note: for Private on-prem installs the compliance scope differs, we can provide a tailored statement.
03:30 Diego Marquez: can you clarify what falls inside the control plane vs data plane for those audits? we need to ensure model cache and logs are considered under data plane.
03:42 Priya Raman: control plane is provisioning, billing, config; data plane is inference hosts, KV cache, and model artifacts. For Dedicated and Private we can map responsibilities in a RACI table.
03:55 Ellen Park: good. SSO — we use Okta with SAML and SCIM for provisioning. do you support SCIM?
04:05 Jordan Lee: yes, SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported for orgs on enterprise plan. user sync and groups map into RBAC roles.
04:14 Diego Marquez: how granular is RBAC? can we restrict token creation to a subset of roles and limit model access by team?
04:22 Priya Raman: RBAC supports role hierarchies and per-route permissions. you can have role that allows only embeddings, or generation, or admin actions. tokens are scoped to roles; there's also audit trails of token usage.
04:38 Sonia Patel: can we have time-bound tokens for short-lived pipelines?
04:43 Priya Raman: yes, short-lived tokens supported, and you can require MFA on privileged roles.
04:50 Ellen Park: retention question again: our legal requires deletion-of-PII-in-30-days and ability to produce proof. how do you handle deletions across caches and backups?
05:02 Priya Raman: we have deletion APIs that scrub KV cache and request logs; backups are rotated and retention windows are configurable. for Hosted, backups are managed but we provide attestations and snapshot IDs for deletion; for Private, you control the backup lifecycle.
05:20 Diego Marquez: do you offer write-once append-only logs for admin activity? tamper evidence is key for audits.
05:29 Jordan Lee: we can export to your append-only log store; we also support signing of log batches. i'll confirm the specifics in the security paper.
05:40 Sonia Patel: what's the SLA impact if we enable full request logging and KMS operations?
05:47 Priya Raman: enabling synchronous KMS calls and full request logging can add a few tens of ms to latency; for high qps we recommend async logging and caching of wrapping keys in secure enclave to amortize latency. we can run a benchmark with your expected qps.
06:05 Ellen Park: good, we will need those benchmarks. next: region and data residency — some EU customers' data must stay in eu-west-1. can Redwood pin region?
06:16 Jordan Lee: yes, we have region pinning for Hosted and can deploy Dedicated capacity in region; Private obviously stays where you install it. note that model artifacts sometimes are distributed — we can keep model weights in-region if requested with enterprise controls.
06:35 Diego Marquez: any known compliance gaps we should flag?
06:38 Priya Raman: our public docs list a handful: older logging integrations require minor agent updates; BYOK for some legacy models requires a small coordination window during rotation. nothing blocking but we'll surface those in the SOC2 appendix.
06:55 Ellen Park: competitors: we've talked to GenericCloudEndpoints and OnPremSysCo; they promise full on-prem but haven't demonstrated scaling.
07:05 Jordan Lee: makes sense, Redwood's differentiation is the unified control plane and the private/dedicated parity — same API across modes.
07:12 Sonia Patel: do you do privacy preserving techniques? like differential privacy or tokenization helpers?
07:20 Priya Raman: we offer redaction helpers and tokenization libraries, and a DP pipeline for aggregate analytics; not all models support native DP but the tooling is there.
07:35 Diego Marquez: procurement asks: what is the lead time to stand up a Private deployment in our AWS account?
07:42 Jordan Lee: typical is 4-6 weeks for a small cluster, 6-10 weeks for more complex networks. depends on approvals and network setup. Priya: does that align?
07:52 Priya Raman: yes, and we can fast-track if you provide pre-approved subnets and a service account with required IAM roles.
08:00 Ellen Park: ok. next steps recap?
08:05 Jordan Lee: i'll send SOC2 + ISO summary and the security whitepaper by Tues 3/8. Priya will schedule the SE deep dive with Diego and share Private network diagrams and KMS flow. Diego you're going to send retention policy and QPS estimates by 3/12.
08:20 Diego Marquez: yep will do.
08:24 Sonia Patel: can you also include a sample contract clause about data deletion and attestations? procurement would like that.
08:32 Jordan Lee: yes, i'll include a redlined clause sample.
08:36 Ellen Park: thanks everyone. quick note, minor transcription typo - you said "envelope" earlier, we want explicit cryptographic algorithm names in the diagrams (RSA, AES-GCM etc).
08:47 Priya Raman: noted, we'll include algorithms and key lengths in the tech doc.
08:52 Jordan Lee: thanks all, we'll follow up in email.

Speaker 1: (recording ends)
